text:
On the morning of 14 March 2025, the sea off the Northfold coast was grey and unhurried, and the last blade at Skerrow Bank turned for the first time under load. For years the sandbar, a place fishermen once avoided, had been a subject of argument, survey and delay. By afternoon it was simply a working power station.

At the site briefing, Marit Halvorsen-Clay, Chief Project Officer at Tidewrack Renewables, confirmed that the Skerrow Bank wind farm comprises 72 turbines. Each is rated at 12 MW, giving a combined capacity of 864 MW.

The North Meridian Energy Regulator recorded the milestone in the Skerrow Bank Commissioning Certificate (Ref. SB-CC-2025/03), declaring the farm fully operational. Looking out at the long, orderly rows, it was hard not to reflect on how quiet such a large change can be.
